summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old woman with a history of mast cell degranulation syndrome, rheumatoid arthritis, orthostatic hypotension, and anxiety presented with acute-onset chest pain, dyspnea, and pruritus following a pulmonary clinic visit. She feared a mast cell crisis but had no objective signs such as rash, hypotension, or hypoxia. Initial treatment in the ER included IV Benadryl, albuterol, and Dilaudid, with symptom recurrence prompting admission. Evaluation showed normal troponins, no EKG changes, and a chest X-ray revealing only chronic findings including resolving organizing pneumonia and atelectasis. Symptoms resolved overnight without further intervention. The clinical course suggested atypical chest pain without evidence of acute cardiac, pulmonary, or mast cell-mediated disease. She was discharged home on her prior medications with follow-up planned with her allergist.
